description: §10.5 condition (a): banned-register tokens in customer copy — the canonical six plus the maintained administrative-formal set. Maintained data, not code. AUDIT-B+1 F12 added the administrative-PROCESS terms after « Dossier en cours d'instruction. » — short, cold, bureaucratic — passed every existing check. ROUND 3 RETREAT, on evidence: « formalité(s) », « procédure(s) » and bare « instruction » were REMOVED because a verifier found honest sentences they refuse — « Pas de formalité compliquée. », « Sans formalités : votre boutique est prête. », « Suivez l'instruction du livreur. ». Negation copy is exactly the promise this product makes to an informal-sector seller. The escape is caught by the PHRASE « cours d'instruction » instead. Also NOT banned: « dossier » and « notification » (honest uses in shipped catalogs). A gate that cries wolf on honest work teaches everyone to disable gates. AUDIT-B+2 F-90 (LISTER-VRAI-1): the match is WHOLE-WORD, so « séquestres », « escrowed » and « conformément aux » all passed while their base forms were refused — §10.5 hard rule 2 bans the WORD, not one spelling of it. Their inflections joined the list (and, on the one verifier pass, the noun « séquestration(s) » and the common verb forms) after being measured against all 2 946 strings of the seven catalogs of the three apps: zero hits, so no honest copy is refused.
